title: Section leaders and the quarrels of later years
summary: As changes came, players resented being told anything, and arguments arose when Cat Anderson was supposed to lead.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Everybody was -- the band came first, in other words.
And then you mean as other additions were made, or other changes were made, you got personalities in there.
And as such personalities were felt and heard.
Well, as changes came along, different guys resent you telling them anything.
And so that's the way it went. You'd let a guy set up there. You wouldn't open your mouth to him. Let him play what he wanted to play.
So nobody in the section would be in command of the section?
Well, yeah. In a way of speaking.

There was always arguments when Cat was there. He was supposed to be in command, and they'd have fights and things, you know, and arguments. But they didn't have that in the days when I'm speaking of.
Yeah. And I guess that same was true of the reed section, I guess.
Well, of course -- I mean, when I think of it -- I haven't thought of it before, but Toby was really the first saxophone, and he was no guy to throw his weight around.
Or lead or dominate a section.
